title: Ramp scaling playbook and KPI sentinels
content:
Summary:
This playbook captures a pragmatic, testable approach to traffic ramping, surge preparedness, and launch KPIs for medium-to-large feature activations (multi-region, multi-model routes). It blends checklist runbooks, a lightweight KPI sentinel dashboard spec, and a small suite of surge-simulation experiments product-ops can run with SRE and serving-runtime before go-live. The goal is to make gating decisions repeatable and narrow the ambiguity around "what to stop for" during early traffic ramps.

Audience:
- Product Ops (owner: Lena Ortega)
- Serving & Runtime (primary SRE + infra contacts)
- Console & Rollouts PMs
- Solutions Eng for customer-specific special cases

High-level ramp philosophy:
1) Incremental capacity-first: prioritize predictable capacity steps over instant full-traffic cutover.
2) Signal-driven gating: use a short list of high-signal KPIs (sentinels) that are easy to compute in near-real-time.
3) Fast rollback boundaries: predefine trigger thresholds and rollback play actions before ramp begins.
4) Confidence through rehearsal: run at least two 'dress rehearsals' (internal traffic + small external beta) and one blast-radius-limited canary.

Core KPI Sentinels (primary gating signals):
- 95th percentile latency (in ms) by route/model: baseline and current window (5m/30m).
- Error rate: >= 5xx + internal validation failures per 1k requests.
- Token cost delta: realized cost per token vs. projection (+/- 10% threshold).
- Quality regression signal: automated eval score on a fixed prompt set (delta >= -3% triggers pause).
- Queue growth rate: pending requests growth > 20% over 10m.
- Downstream SLA impact: percent of dependent routes failing (if > 3 routes show degradation, escalate).

Secondary metrics (contextual, not immediate gates):
- Throughput per GPU (tokens/sec) vs expected.
- KV cache hit rate and prefix reuse.
- Autoscaler churn: number of scale events per 15 minutes.
- Cost burn-rate vs committed budget.

Pre-launch checklist (week-by-week):
- T-3w: run traffic profile analysis. Owners: product-ops + serving-runtime. Deliverable: expected token-per-minute curve and bucketed sequence length distribution.
- T-2w: capacity carve (dedicated pools or host planning) and quota assignments. Deliverable: reservation confirmation + runbook link.
- T-10d: automated eval suite baseline collected (test prompts + expected outputs).
- T-7d: internal dry-run #1 (traffic generator, synthetic users). Run till steady-state for 2 hours at target 10% traffic. Capture sentinels.
- T-4d: remediation iteration (fix slow kernels, adjust batchers, tune KV policies).
- T-3d: internal dry-run #2 at 25% with mixed sequence lengths.
- T-2d: external beta (subset of customers or controlled flag).
- T-1d: final health check and stakeholder go/no-go sync.

Runbook: immediate actions for sentinel breaches:
- If 95p latency breaches threshold for 5m:
  - Step 1: Engage runtime on-call, set routing policy to route 30% to fallback model (manual toggle).
  - Step 2: Increase autoscaler headroom by +20% (if allowed by dedicated pool).
  - Step 3: If latency still elevated after 10m, rollback canary and revert traffic to previous model version; open incident and notify stakeholders.
- If error rate crosses threshold:
  - Step 1: Disable incremental features (safety flags) and revert to baseline prompt templates.
  - Step 2: If errors are 5xx infrastructure related, immediately spike capacity for affected zone and throttle ingestion; initiate SRE postmortem prep.
- If quality eval delta below acceptable:
  - Step 1: Halt rollout at current step; trigger product-quality triage with model-owner, PM, and ML-research.
  - Step 2: Consider fallback routing to previous model variant and reduce batch sizes to check for determinism issues.

Surge simulation matrix (quick experiments to run in preflight):
- Burst test: 2x peak QPS for 10 minutes, observe queue growth and autoscaler latency.
- Sustained high throughput: 0.8x projected peak for 1 hour to verify thermal behavior and kernel stability.
- Mixed-length pattern: alternate long/short seq patterns to test KV cache and prefix reuse.
- Failure injection: drop 10% of backend responses to emulate partial zone failures and verify graceful fallback paths.

Decision ladder (example thresholds for moving from step N to N+1 traffic):
- From 0% -> 10%: all primary sentinels green for 30m.
- 10% -> 25%: sustained 95p latency within +5% of baseline for 1h, error rate < 0.5% over baseline.
- 25% -> 50%: quality eval drift <= -1% and cost variance within +7% for 2h.
- 50% -> 100%: no sentinel regressions for 4h and SRE agrees on steady-state stability.

Stakeholder roles and contact tree:
- Product Ops lead (owner): Lena Ortega — overall decision authority for non-green go/no-go.
- Runtime lead: Samir Patel — responsible for autoscaler, routing toggles, and kernel rollbacks.
- SRE on-call: Jonah Kim — incident commander during ramp window.
- Model owner: Dr. Priya Nair — quality triage and model rollback authorization.
- Customer Success escalation: Maya Li — customer notifications and handoffs.

Canary configuration templates (recommended defaults):
- Canary A: 5% traffic, isolated region, retention of previous model for instant fallback. Duration: 2 hours.
- Canary B: 20% traffic, multi-AZ split, run continuous quality evals every 15 minutes. Duration: 4 hours.

Post-launch checklist (first 72h):
- Hourly snapshot of the primary sentinels + a short summary to #launch-ops.
- 6h post-launch: team sync with SRE and runtime to review any anomalous signals.
- 24h: curated sample of 200 end-to-end requests for manual quality review.
- 72h: retrospective and 'lessons-captured' doc; formalize any playbook changes.

Lightweight KPI sentinel dashboard spec (implementation notes):
- Panel: 95p latency by route (5m/30m) — alert threshold config.
- Panel: error rate (5xx + model failure classes) with counts and rolling windows.
- Panel: queue length and average wait time.
- Panel: automated eval score delta with link to failing prompt examples.
- Slack webhook on sentinel breach with structured payload: {route, metric, value, timeframe, link-to-playbook}.

Quick references & shortcuts:
- Run traffic generator: scripts/traffic_gen/run.sh --profile ramp-10pct --duration 60m (see linked GH PR).
- Toggle fallback routing: Console > Rollouts > Route > set fallback:previous-model (runtime lead privilege).
- Emergency rollback: Git tag revert and route switch command (SRE-run only).

Open questions to resolve before final signoff:
- Exact budget headroom allowed for autoscaling in Dedicated pools (finance signoff needed).
- Confirm which customer cohorts are eligible for Beta (solutions eng to provide list).
- Agree on the final prompt-eval suite and acceptance score thresholds with Applied ML.

Appendix: example quick play snippets (for on-call):
- Check 95th latency: curl https://metrics-api.internal/v1/query?metric=latency_95p&route=route-x
- Scale up headroom: runtime-cli scale --pool=dedicated-pool-X --delta=+20%
- Switch fallback: runtime-cli route set --route=route-x --policy=fallback:previous-model

Notes and provenance:
- This doc is a pragmatic synthesis of product-ops practice, SRE ramp lessons, and serving-runtime constraints; it intentionally favors a short sentinel list to avoid alert fatigue.
- Refs: Confluence Ramp Model Profiles (linked), past incident review (JIRA-PROD-2871).

Next steps (owner actions):
- Lena: schedule two dress rehearsals with SRE and runtime in the next 10 days.
- Samir: confirm dedicated pool carve and publish autoscaler headroom policy.
- Priya: finalize automated eval prompts and baseline scores.

Revision history:
- 2024-09-12: draft (initial checklist and sentinel list).
- 2024-10-03: added surge simulation matrix after SRE feedback.
- 2025-02-09: updated thresholds for decision ladder and added post-launch cadence.

End of document.
